headline: Approved a Vote Mob/Cash Mob at the Bristol Farmers Market to gather business nominations for the fourth-quarter Cash Mob.
summary: Members shared community event updates and discussed plans for a Vote Mob at the Bristol Farmers Market. They approved a motion to hold the Vote Mob and collect nominations on September 19, 2026. The Passport item was continued to the September 2026 agenda.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the June 23, 2026 meeting. All present members were in favor.
Approved a Vote Mob/Cash Mob for the Bristol Farmers Market on September 19, 2026, with a volunteer nomination sheet for the fourth quarter Cash Mob. All present members were in favor.
Continued the Diversity Council Passport next steps to the September 2026 agenda.
Agreed to again provide refreshments at the fourth quarter Unity in the Community event, paid by individual donations.

decision_titles: Vote Mob/Cash Mob for the Bristol Farmers Market
Refreshments for the fourth quarter Unity in the Community event
plain_text:
Diversity Council Meeting 
Tuesday, August 25, 2026 at 6:30pm 
Meeting Room 1-2, City Hall, 111 N. Main Street & on Zoom 
 
Present:  Interim Chair Marcus Patton, Council Members Sandy Kamens, David 
Rackliffe, Carolyn Palmquist, and Danny Palmquist 
Absent: Council Members Jeff Israel and Tony Lopes 
Guests: None 
 
I. Call to Order 
The Interim Chair called the meeting to order at 6:32pm. 
 
II. Council Attendance 
        A round table roll call of the Council Members was taken. There was a quorum. 
 
III. Public Participation 
There was no Public Participation. 
 
IV. Approval of Minutes 
a. Meeting Minutes from the June 23, 2026 Meeting 
The Interim Chair called for a Motion to approve the Minutes from the June 23, 
2026 Meeting. Council Member Kamens made the motion to approve the 
Minutes. The motion was seconded by Council Member Carolyn Palmquist. All 
were in favor and the Minutes were accepted into the record. 
 
V. Current Business 
a. Council Members Review Resource and Event News and Notes  
Council Members provided the following updates: 
 
Interim Chair Patton:  
Attended the Hubbell School backpack event. It was a true family get-together 
and attendance was high. Payton’s Promise made a large donation of school 
supplies to fill the backpacks.
The Interim Chair attended an event at Real Café when Gov. Lamont was in 
Bristol that day meeting with residents and business owners. The Governor 
responded to questions about AI and other concerns. 
 
Council Member Rackliffe: 
Attended the City Council Meeting where the Flock and Red Light/Speed 
Cameras were on the agenda. Current concerns such as retention capabilities 
of the Flock cameras were discussed, as well as cyber security controls. He 
made a point to clarify that current City Ordinances don’t address the use of 
Flock cameras. The Flock cameras do help the police coordinate their efforts 
across district lines.  
 
The Council Member also noted that new donations have come into the Men and 
Boys Club which he is associated with, and the donation from Barnes increased 
from $5,000 to $10,000. 
 
Council Member Carolyn Palmquist: 
Reported on recent Bristol Pride events including a Dungeons & Dragons night at 
Faith Lutheran Church which was a free-to-attend community connections 
event. Dark Moon on N. Main Street contributed to the event. 
 
The upcoming Bristol Pride Fall Fantasy Ball on October 23rd is looking for a new 
host location as Ventana’s has closed and they were the original venue. The 
group is looking into having a table at the September 19th Farmers Market the 
day of the Diversity Council’s Vote Mob for the Market, and the No Boundaries 
Youth Academy in New Britain held their Addams Family play. 
 
b. Cash Mob/Vote Mob Review and Ideas 
Logistics for the Vote Mob to benefit the Bristol Farmer Market with the people’s 
choice online standing were discussed. Cross promotional branding will be 
used to incorporate the Diversity Council with the Farmers Market. The flyer and 
promoting the voting will start as soon as possible ahead of the September 19th 
Vote Mob Day at the market. The last day to vote is September 30th. 
 
The voting rules emphasize one vote per email address. Voters can access the 
voting site through the provided QR Code or a link. As of this meeting, the Bristol 
Farmers Market has 138 votes. Council Member Carolyn Palmquist will create
the co-branded flyer, review it with the Farmers Market contacts and with the 
Interim Chair for approval, and then it will be publicized. 
 
Discussion followed, including the best way forward to best gather nominations 
and votes for the next Cash Mob in support of an area business. Based on the 
discussion, the following Motion was made: 
 
Motion to conduct a Vote Mob/Cash Mob for the Bristol Farmers Market at the 
regularly scheduled market day of Saturday, September 19, 2026, and provide a 
volunteer nomination sheet at the event to gather business names for the fourth 
quarter Cash Mob. Based on the number of nominations received on that day, 
the Diversity Council will decide whether to open up nominations on Bristol 
Talks to allow for more options, or move ahead with the voting based on the 
nominations already received.  
 
The motion was made by Council Member Carolyn Palmquist and seconded by 
Council Member Rackliffe. There was no additional discussion or questions. All 
were in favor and the motion passed into the record. 
 
c. Tee-Shirt Orders 
The Diversity Council shirt orders will ideally be made and arrive for the Council 
to wear at the Vote Mob event on September 19th. 
 
VI. New Business 
a. Final Cash Mob '26 Options 
The Interim Chair noted this item was included in the earlier discussion under V. 
New Business b. Cash Mob/Vote Mob Review and Ideas. 
 
b. Diversity Council "Passport" Next Steps 
This item will be on the September 2026 Agenda as the members continue to 
consider the information and discussion reviewed at an earlier meeting. 
 
The Interim Chair noted wanting to also add the conversation about youth 
involvement in the Council to the September meeting. Members were asked to 
consider options for incorporating the area high schools and teens into the 
Council, and/or how the Council can best support the school’s existing diversity 
programs and/or efforts. Discussion followed including including the need to
ensure that all three high schools were represented, as well as inviting 
Superintendent Iris White back for additional discussion. 
 
c. Unity in the Community Execution 
Members were also asked to consider ideas and platforms for the fourth quarter 
Unity in the Community event. The Bristol Public Library allows the Council to 
use their space free of cost, with a small fee for after event clean up if food is 
provided. The Council agreed they would again provide refreshments paid by 
their individual donations. Discussion followed regarding some possible topics 
and logistics. The Council’s goal is to ensure they’re serving the community in 
the best way possible in this year end gathering. 
 
VII. Adjournment 
With no further items noted, the Interim Chair called for a motion to adjourn. The 
motion was made by Council Member Rackcliffe and was seconded by Council 
Member Kamens. All were in favor and the meeting adjourned at 8:21pm. 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
 
Sharon Arsego 
Recording Secretary
